subproblems.title: Mass of a difference is at most the sum of the masses (fact (F1); Simon Ch. 6, 2.5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, G ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets and let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Then M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) in [0, ∞]. Conventions: 𝒟_n(U) is the space of n-currents in U (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n) and 𝒟ⁿ(U) the test n-forms in U (TestFormOn U n: smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U, a submodule of the space of forms); |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are called admissible for M_G; massAdmissibleOn U n G); A − B is the contract instance Sub, whose underlying linear functional is ω ↦ A(ω) − B(ω).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (A - B).massOn G ≤ A.massOn G + B.massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F1) of the parent proof, i.e. the triangle inequality for Simon's mass 6.2.5 (M_G is a supremum over admissible forms), as used in Simon's proof of Theorem 6.7.2.
1. By definition M_G(A − B) = sup{ofReal((A − B)(ω)) : ω admissible for M_G}. By the least-upper-bound property (sSup_le) it suffices to fix an admissible ω and prove ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B).
2. −ω is admissible for M_G. Indeed 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a submodule, so −ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and its underlying form is the pointwise negative of the underlying form of ω. Hence tsupport(−ω) = tsupport(ω) ⊆ G (tsupport_neg), and for every x, |(−ω)(x)| = |−(ω(x))| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1, because the Euclidean coefficient norm is invariant under negation (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
3. (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) by the definition of the contract instance Sub, and B(−ω) = −B(ω) because the underlying functional of B is linear. Hence (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω).
4. For real s, t one has ofReal(s + t) ≤ ofReal(s) + ofReal(t) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le). With step 3, ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ ofReal(A(ω)) + ofReal(B(−ω)).
5. Every admissible value is bounded by the corresponding mass (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn): ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) because ω is admissible, and ofReal(B(−ω)) ≤ M_G(B) because −ω is admissible by step 2. Adding these two bounds to step 4 gives ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B); by step 1, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to one admissible ω, since M_G(A − B) is a supremum over admissible forms.
−ω is admissible: the same topological support and a negation-invariant Euclidean coefficient norm.
(A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω), and ofReal is subadditive.
Bound ofReal(A(ω)) by M_G(A) and ofReal(B(−ω)) by M_G(B).

subproblems.title: The restriction of an integer multiplicity current to an open subdomain is integer multiplicity
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U, V ⊆ ℝ^P with V ⊆ U (proof hVU) and V open. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity, i.e. T is represented by some IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U (Simon 6.3.1). Then the restriction T⌞V = T.restrictDomain hVU ∈ 𝒟_n(V), defined by T⌞V(ω) = T(ιω), is integer multiplicity in V. (Remark: the proof exhibits the representing triple (M ∩ V, θ, ξ).) This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.restrict_im-a1), which is reused. Conventions: 𝒟_n(D) is the space of n-currents in D (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn D n) and 𝒟ⁿ(D) the test n-forms in D (TestFormOn D n: smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in D); ι = testFormOnInclusion hVU n regards ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) as an element of 𝒟ⁿ(U) with the same underlying form; Hⁿ = μHE[n]; an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in D (contract structure IMRep D n) consists of a Borel, countably n-rectifiable set M ⊆ D, a measurable θ : ℝ^P → ℕ with θ > 0 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D, and an Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable ξ (values n-vectors, i.e. continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) such that for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q; R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x); R represents X ∈ 𝒟_n(D) when X(ω) = R.action(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(D), and X is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity X) when some IMRep in D represents it; HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) means finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0+, where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V : Set (Euclid P)) (hVU : V ⊆ U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity (T.restrictDomain hVU)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 and 2.16, with Ch. 3, 1.4 (approximate tangent planes are local). This is the integer multiplicity clause of fact (F2) of the parent proof, proved directly for every open V ⊆ U instead of through (IR).
Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U representing T and put R' := (M ∩ V, θ, ξ). Steps 1–7 check the fields of an IMRep in V; step 8 proves the representation.
1. Measurability: M is Borel and V is open, hence Borel, so M ∩ V is Borel.
2. M ∩ V ⊆ V.
3. Rectifiability: M ∩ V ⊆ M and M is countably n-rectifiable, so M ∩ V is countably n-rectifiable: the null set and the countably many Lipschitz images covering M also cover M ∩ V (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
4. θ is measurable, and θ(x) > 0 for every x ∈ M ∩ V ⊆ M.
5. Local integrability in V: let K be compact with K ⊆ V. Then (M ∩ V) ∩ K = M ∩ K because K ⊆ V, and K ⊆ V ⊆ U, so ∫_{(M∩V)∩K} θ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the local integrability of R in U.
6. ξ is Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. strongly measurable, because Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono; AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
7. Orientation. Claim: if x ∈ V and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ V) x Q. The condition finrank Q = n does not involve M. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Since V is open choose s > 0 with B_s(x) ⊆ V, and since spt f is compact choose L > 0 with spt f ⊆ B_L(0). Let 0 < r < s/L. If y ∈ B_L(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(M), say y = r⁻¹(z − x) with z ∈ M, then |z − x| = r|y| < rL < s, so z ∈ B_s(x) ⊆ V and y ∈ η_{x,r}(M ∩ V); together with M ∩ V ⊆ M this gives B_L(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(M) = B_L(0) ∩ η_{x,r}(M ∩ V). Because f vanishes outside the open, hence Borel, ball B_L(0), every set A satisfies ∫_A f dHⁿ = ∫_{B_L(0)∩A} f dHⁿ (restrict Hⁿ⌞A further to B_L(0): Measure.restrict_restrict and setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). Applied to A = η_{x,r}(M) and A = η_{x,r}(M ∩ V), this gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(M∩V)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ for every r ∈ (0, s/L), a neighbourhood of 0 in (0, ∞). The right side tends to ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0+, hence so does the left side (Tendsto.congr'). This proves the claim. (Remark: the accepted Lean proof of this reused declaration obtains the claim from its own accepted dependency dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff, node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.approx_tangent_local-a1, which allows an Hⁿ-null modification of M near x; here the removed set M ∖ (M ∩ V) does not meet V at all, so the special case is proved directly above.)
   By the orientation field of R, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. A property holding Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. also holds Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), and Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ V (ae_restrict_mem; M ∩ V is measurable). For such an x we have x ∈ V, so the claim gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ V) x Q, and the same Q satisfies IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. Hence R' is an IMRep in V.
8. Representation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). Since ιω has the same underlying form as ω, T⌞V(ω) = T(ιω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x). For x ∈ M ∖ (M ∩ V) we have x ∉ V ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and the integrand θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) vanishes (ξ(x) is linear). M is measurable and M ∩ V ⊆ M, so ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩V} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero), and the right side is R'.action(ω). Thus R' represents T⌞V, and T⌞V is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict a representation (M, θ, ξ) of T to (M ∩ V, θ, ξ); measurability, rectifiability, positivity and local integrability on compact subsets of V ⊆ U are inherited.
Approximate tangent planes are local: for x in the open set V the blow-ups of M and M ∩ V agree on the support of any test function for small r, so the orientation condition transfers.
Forms supported in V vanish on M ∖ V, so the integral over M equals the integral over M ∩ V.

subproblems.title: Mass on W is determined by the action on forms supported in W, across a change of domain
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, V, W ⊆ ℝ^P with V ⊆ U (proof hVU) and W ⊆ V, and let S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and S' ∈ 𝒟_n(V). Suppose S(ιω) = S'(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Then M_W(S) = M_W(S'). This is, with the identical frozen Lean type, the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_massOn_eq_of_agreeOn (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.mass_agree-a1), which is reused. Conventions: 𝒟_n(D) is the space of n-currents in D (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn D n) and 𝒟ⁿ(D) the test n-forms in D (TestFormOn D n: smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in D); ι = testFormOnInclusion hVU n regards ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) as an element of 𝒟ⁿ(U) with the same underlying form; |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector (covectorEuclideanNorm); for X ∈ 𝒟_n(D), M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(D) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y (massAdmissibleOn D n W).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V W : Set (Euclid P)) (hVU : V ⊆ U) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (S' : GeometricCurrentOn V n), W ⊆ V → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → S (testFormOnInclusion hVU n ω) = S' ω) → S.massOn W = S'.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.5 read with the terminology 2.16 (T₁ = T₂ in W). This gives the mass clause of fact (F2) of the parent proof.
Notation. For D ⊆ ℝ^P let A_D(W) = massAdmissibleOn D n W = {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(D) : tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y}. Thus M_W(S) = sup{ofReal(S(ω)) : ω ∈ A_U(W)} and M_W(S') = sup{ofReal(S'(ω')) : ω' ∈ A_V(W)}. The map ι keeps the underlying form (testFormOnInclusion_coe).
1. Put I := {ofReal(S(ω)) : ω ∈ A_U(W)} and I' := {ofReal(S'(ω')) : ω' ∈ A_V(W)}. Since M_W(S) = sup I and M_W(S') = sup I', it suffices to prove I = I'.
2. I ⊆ I'. Let ω ∈ A_U(W). Its underlying form is a test form (IsTestForm), and tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ V, so the same form defines an element ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). Both conditions defining A_V(W) concern only the underlying form, so ω' ∈ A_V(W). Also ιω' = ω, since both have the same underlying form (Subtype.ext). The hypothesis applied to ω' (tsupport ω' = tsupport ω ⊆ W) gives S(ω) = S(ιω') = S'(ω'). Hence ofReal(S(ω)) = ofReal(S'(ω')) ∈ I'.
3. I' ⊆ I. Let ω' ∈ A_V(W) and ω := ιω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). It has the same underlying form as ω', so ω ∈ A_U(W), and the hypothesis gives S(ω) = S'(ω'). Hence ofReal(S'(ω')) = ofReal(S(ω)) ∈ I.
4. By steps 2 and 3, I = I', so M_W(S) = sup I = sup I' = M_W(S'). ∎
proof_key_steps: Each mass M_W is the supremum of ofReal of the current's values on the admissible forms supported in W.
Because W ⊆ V ⊆ U, the admissible forms for U and for V are the same underlying forms, related by testFormOnInclusion.
The hypothesis gives equal values on corresponding forms, so the two value sets coincide and the suprema are equal.
